author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell breaks down the strange new reality of self checkout machines prompting customers for tips, right as inflation has already driven costs up, leaving people wondering where that money even goes. He points out that even tips given to actual human employees aren't always guaranteed to reach them, so when it's a robot with no legal precedent requiring the tip go anywhere, that money almost certainly just gets added straight to corporate profit. Russell argues this is part of a much bigger pattern, wealth and revenue being quietly extracted from ordinary people and funneled to the very top of a very tall pyramid, often by powerful transnational organizations that avoid paying tax altogether. A sharp, infuriating look at corporate greed hiding in plain sight.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest lays out a theory that the pandemic was planned in advance, but pulled forward into 2020 only after every effort to remove Trump through other means had failed. They argue the one thing that saved the rest of us was that the plan wasn't fully in place yet, certain states and even entire countries hadn't been brought under centralized control, giving people a genuine choice rather than a mandate. Those outliers became an accidental case study, showing lower deaths in places that never fully locked down, proof the guest says exposes the whole thing as a failure rather than the success it's still remembered as by many. A sharp, unsettling breakdown of what might have happened if the plan had gone exactly as intended.
